newsitem.title: UK: BOE restructure not enough for EMU - analysts.
newsitem.headline: BOE restructure not enough for EMU - analysts.

text.p: Sweeping proposals announced on Tuesday to restructure the Bank of England are in no way enough to satisfy the criteria laid down by the Maastricht Treaty, said Graham Bishop, adviser on European financial affairs at Salomon Brothers.
"This is not enough. The Bank has to be made entirely independent and the government has retained its right to issue instructions," he told Reuters.
But Bishop, a leading expert on EMU and adviser to the Treasury Committee in the House of Commons, said this was a big step in the direction of satisfying the conditions laid down for EMU.

"This is a building block, a launch pad. It may be that the legislation will only need a short clause to be added -- in which the government gives up its residual right to instruct -- in order to satisfy Maastricht," he said.
Bishop said once the Bank of England legislation is published it will be possible to measure the ease with which such a clause can be added.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced radical changes to the mechanics of setting monetary policy on Tuesday. The Bank of England will set interest rates independently of government and have its own exchange reserves to help steer policy.
A new monetary policy committee will be formed with nine members including four government appointees and a second deputy governor.
Martin Brookes, international economist at Goldman Sachs, agreed the new legislation stops short of Maastricht terms.

"The provision in the proposed legislation for a possible government override of the Bank's independence appears to contravene article 107 of the Maastricht Treaty, which states that the government cannot instruct central banks," he told Reuters.

"Nevertheless, the legislation could be easily be amended in time to qualify for EMU and the changes announced today are an enormous leap towards a fully independent Bank of England, consistent with entry into monetary union."
